sources.text: A buffer contains a weak acid HA and its conjugate base A−. Small additions of strong acid consume A− to form HA. Strong base consumes HA. Buffering limits pH change within capacity; it does not mean pH 7.

objectives.label: Predict which buffer species reacts with an added strong acid or base

items.stem: An HF/F− buffer receives a small addition of HCl. Choose HF or F− as the species consumed; explain in one or two sentences.
items.hint: Added HCl supplies H+. Which species can accept it?

key.explanation: F− accepts H+ from HCl and forms HF, so a small addition changes pH only a little (C §buffer). The explanation field is shown against the source but is not scored.

feedback.correct: F− is the keyed species. C §buffer explains its reaction with added acid. This is a check of species selection; it does not establish all of buffer chemistry.
feedback.incorrect: Added strong acid consumes the conjugate base F−, forming HF (C §buffer).
